Told that an imam's long prayers kept a man away, the Prophet angrily said whoever leads people must shorten the prayer, for among them are the sick, weak and needy.
The Prophet led prayer from the pulpit, stepping down to prostrate, and, injured by a fall from a horse, led it sitting, saying the imam is to be followed.
Congregational prayer is twenty-five times better than prayer alone; each step to the mosque raises a degree and erases a sin, and angels pray for one waiting at his place.
Come to the prayer calmly, not hurrying, pray what you catch and complete what you missed; at the Iqama do not stand until you see the Prophet.
After the Iqama the Prophet, being junub, told the people to keep their places, bathed and returned with his head dripping to lead the prayer.
After the Iqama the Prophet kept talking quietly with a man in a corner of the mosque, delaying the prayer until some people dozed.
The Prophet nearly burned the houses of men absent from congregational prayer, which is twenty-five or twenty-seven times better than praying alone; Abu ad-Darda found only it still kept up.
Fajr and Isha are heaviest for the hypocrites, and the Prophet nearly burned the houses of the absent; two people should give the Adhan and Iqama, the elder leading.
The Prophet rebuked a man praying two rak'at after the Iqama of Fajr had been called, asking whether Fajr has four rak'at.
On cold, rainy or muddy days the caller said 'Pray in your homes'; the Prophet prayed at the homes of blind Itban and a heavy Ansari, and prostrated in mud.
Abu Bakr stepped back when the Prophet arrived during his prayer, and men should say Subhan Allah rather than clap; the eldest leads; the Prophet led Itban's household when visiting.
The imam is to be followed: bow, rise and prostrate after him, and sit if he sits; companions waited until he prostrated; one rising before him risks a donkey's head.
Salim, a slave knowing most Quran, led the first emigrants; obey a chief even if Ethiopian; an imam's mistake is his own; Uthman: share people's good deeds, avoid their bad.
Staying at Maimuna's house, Ibn Abbas stood at the Prophet's left in the night prayer and was drawn round to his right.
An imam should keep the prayer short for the weak, old and needy: the Prophet rebuked Mu'adh for reciting Al-Baqara, and shortened his own prayer on hearing a child cry.
Straighten the rows, shoulder to shoulder, for the Prophet sees behind him; if people knew the first row's reward they would draw lots for it; Anas found Medina's rows unaligned.
The Prophet moved Ibn Abbas from his left to his right; Anas and an orphan stood behind the Prophet, with Umm Sulaim alone behind them.
After falling from a horse the Prophet led seated and said the imam is to be followed in Takbir, bowing, rising and prostration.
Ill or hurt by a fall, the Prophet prayed sitting, signalled those standing behind him to sit, and said the imam is to be followed in Takbir, bowing and rising.
Prayer in congregation is over twenty times better than at home or market; each step to the mosque raises a degree, and angels pray for one awaiting prayer.
The Prophet says he intended to have the Iqama called and then burn the houses of those who do not attend the prayer.
While the Prophet made peace among Bani Amr bin Auf, Abu Bakr led the prayer and stepped back when he came; men should say Subhan Allah, clapping being for women.
Congregational prayer is twenty-five times better than praying alone, and the angels of night and day gather at Fajr, whose recitation the verse calls witnessed.
Staying at Maimuna's, Ibn Abbas stood on the Prophet's left in the night prayer, and the Prophet took him by his locks of hair and moved him to his right.
When Mu'adh called a man a hypocrite for leaving his long Surat al-Baqara prayer, the Prophet rebuked Mu'adh for burdening people and told him to recite shorter surahs.
When the imam says Amin all should say it, for whoever's Amin coincides with the angels' has his past sins forgiven.
Angered that an imam's lengthy prayer kept a man from the morning congregation, the Prophet told imams to shorten it, for among the people are the old, weak and busy.
Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhaifa, led the early emigrants and companions, among them Abu Bakr and Umar, in prayer at the Quba mosque.
While the Prophet made peace among Bani Amr, Abu Bakr led the prayer and stepped back on his arrival; in prayer, men say Subhan Allah to alert and women clap.
The Prophet said he almost ordered the houses of men absent from congregational prayer burned, and that they would come to Isha for a meaty bone.
